title: Lamb of God (Matthew 8:8)
hookLine: the bread is broken and all say Lord, I am not worthy, only say the word
last: SO BE IT, ALL OF US.

cards: His servant was sick at home. Jesus offered to come. And this army officer, a centurion, a powerful man used to giving orders, said no.
Don't come. I'm not worthy to have you under my roof. Just say the word, and he'll be healed.
Jesus marveled, and said he had not found faith so great, not even in Israel. You met him back on day thirty-nine.
At Mass, just before communion, Catholics say that soldier's words: an outsider's sentence, on the lips of a whole church.

teach.b: After the Our Father, people turn and offer each other a sign of peace, a handshake, a nod, a hug for family. Then the priest takes the large host and breaks it.

That breaking is old: in the book of Acts, the first Christians gather for the breaking of bread. He drops a small piece into the chalice, bread and wine together again. And while he does, everyone sings: Agnus Dei.
Lamb of God. In Latin: Agnus Dei, qui tollis peccata mundi, miserere nobis. Lamb of God, who take away the sins of the world, have mercy on us.

teach.h: LAMB OF GOD, GRANT US PEACE.
teach.b: And at the last, instead of mercy: dona nobis pacem, grant us peace.
Why a lamb? Because of John the Baptist. When he saw Jesus coming toward him, he said, in the Douay-Rheims: "Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who taketh away the sin of the world."

Some readers hear in it the Passover lamb, whose blood marked the doors in Egypt on the night of freedom. Then the priest lifts the broken host and says John's words, and the people answer with the centurion's.
In the Douay-Rheims the officer says: "Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldst enter under my roof: but only say the word, and my servant shall be healed."
At Mass, one word changes. Not my servant. My soul.
Catholics say it about themselves. They hear honesty in it: nobody earns this. And hope: one word from him is enough.

how: After the sign of peace the priest breaks the consecrated host while the congregation sings the Agnus Dei; he then raises it with John the Baptist's words, and all respond with the centurion's words from Matthew 8:8, adapted to 'my soul shall be healed'.

games.q: you're the centurion. your servant is sick, and Jesus offers to come to your house. what do you say?
o: I'm not worthy to have you under my roof; only say the word.
send one of your disciples instead.
games.why: "Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldst enter under my roof: but only say the word, and my servant shall be healed." Jesus said he had not found so great faith in Israel.

practice: An old instruction, credited to Saint Cyril of Jerusalem, tells people coming to communion to make the left hand a throne for the right, because the right is about to receive a king.

Rest your right hand in your left, palms up and empty: nothing in them, nothing earned. If you pray, say the centurion's sentence quietly, the way Catholics do before communion; if you don't, just keep your hands open and still.

wordCard.voice: Agnus Dei. Latin for Lamb of God: the song as the bread is broken, from John the Baptist's words about Jesus. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: Lamb of God, the chant sung as the bread is broken.

carryVoice: Your line: only say the word. Feeling unworthy doesn't have to keep something good out. Day one hundred sixteen, done.
